summary.text: Energy is the quantity transferred to a body or system, seen in the ability to do work and in heat and light.
It takes forms such as kinetic, potential, elastic, chemical and radiant, and its SI unit is the joule.
Energy is conserved: the total in an isolated system stays constant, though it can change from one form to another.

facts.label: Potential energy
facts.value: Based on position in a field or stored

facts.label: Mechanical energy
facts.value: Kinetic plus potential energy in a system

items.prompt: Physicists say every form of energy, even chemical, can be sorted into two broad groups. Which two?

options.label: Energy of motion and energy of position or storage
Energy you can see and energy you cannot
Natural energy and energy people make
Energy of heat and energy of light

items.explain: Kinetic and potential energy are sufficient to describe all forms of energy.

items.prompt: Why is a drawn bowstring said to hold energy before it is released?

options.label: Strings generate energy as they stretch
The deformed solid stores elastic energy
Tension turns directly into heat
The archer's breath is stored inside

items.explain: Elastic energy is stored in a solid object that has been deformed.

items.prompt: A campfire burns a log to ash. What happens to the log's chemical energy?

options.label: It vanishes as the wood is used up
It is converted into a larger amount of energy
It is converted, mostly to heat and light, and the total is conserved
It stays stored in the ash left behind

items.explain: Energy cannot be destroyed, only converted in form, and energy shows up as heat and light.

items.prompt: At the top of its path a swing mostly has stored energy of position, and at the bottom mostly motion. What is the sum of those two called?

options.label: Nuclear energy
Radiant energy
Internal energy
Mechanical energy

items.explain: The sum of kinetic and potential energy within a system is referred to as mechanical energy.

items.prompt: In 1905 Einstein showed that an object's rest mass corresponds to what?

options.label: A fixed amount of heat
An equivalent amount of rest energy
An unchanging amount of motion
A set amount of light it must give off

items.explain: Special relativity showed that rest mass corresponds to an equivalent amount of rest energy.

items.prompt: Suppose an experiment gave different results on Monday than on Friday. Which law would that threaten?

options.label: Conservation of rest mass
The idea that heat is a substance
Conservation of energy
The idea that energy has a unit

items.explain: Conservation of energy follows from the fact that the laws of physics do not change over time.
